name: Michigan

statute.readVia: https://web.archive.org/web/20260208080357/https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=mcl-257-709 (archived copy of the official page dated 2026-02-08, "MCL complete through PA 74 of 2025"; legislature.mi.gov refused our connection)

windshield.strip: tinted film only along the top edge, not more than 4 inches from the top of the windshield or lower than the shade band, whichever is closer to the top

frontSide.note: MCL 257.709(1)(a) bars any film or window application on the side windows immediately adjacent to the driver or front passenger, except a tinted film along the top edge that does not extend more than 4 inches from the top. No percentage is written in the law.

backSide.note: no transmittance limit; material may not create a total solar reflectance of 35% or more in the visible light range (MCL 257.709(1)(b)); two outside mirrors needed if the rear view is obstructed (257.709(2))

rear.note: same 35% solar reflectance limit; two outside rearview mirrors required when the rear window is obstructed (MCL 257.709(2))

reflectivity.back: total solar reflectance under 35% in the visible light range

medicalExemption.text: Special window treatment or application determined necessary by a physician or optometrist for a light-sensitive or photosensitive person, if the owner or operator has in possession a letter signed by the physician or optometrist indicating that it is a medical necessity; it may not interfere with or obstruct the driver's clear vision of the highway (MCL 257.709(3)(e)).

penalty.text: Civil infraction under the Michigan Vehicle Code; the fine amount is not written in 257.709 and was not read

quotes: upon or in the front windshield, the side windows immediately adjacent to the driver or front passenger, or the sidewings adjacent to and forward of the driver or front passenger

except that a tinted film may be used along the top edge of the windshield ... if the material does not extend more than 4 inches from the top of the windshield or lower than the shade band, whichever is closer to the top of the windshield
a material that creates a total solar reflectance of 35% or more in the visible light range
if the owner or operator of a motor vehicle has in possession a letter signed by a physician or optometrist, indicating that the special window treatment or application is a medical necessity

radarDetector.note: No Michigan ban on radar detectors in passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)
